page: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is a cloud server instance belonging to the Regular Purpose family, configured with 16 shared x86_64 vCPUs backed by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA extensions. Memory allocation totals 31.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 1.95 GB of memory per core. The instance provides 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, contains no hardware GPU accelerators, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

Benchmark results show strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording 3016.68 in single-core testing and Geekbench delivering a single-core score of 1760.0. Multi-core execution achieves a stress-ng score of 48080.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12028.0, supported by PassMark CPU results of 34399.09. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 206.52 GB/s, positioning it in the top performance quartile. In workload-specific metrics, compilation with Clang reaches 22255.0 points on Geekbench, Redis SET throughput registers at 34.09 million operations per second, and medium 7B model LLM text generation reaches 32.09 tokens per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory profile delivers dense compute and generous NVMe capacity relative to operational expenditure, making it cost-efficient for core-heavy workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools. However, because the instance relies on a shared CPU allocation model, consistent sustained peak execution may experience variance under multi-tenant host contention. Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is well configured for build systems, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application serving, batch text processing, and intermediate database caching.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is an x86_64 cloud server featuring 16 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz, 31.0 GB of system memory, and 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The AMD EPYC architecture features hardware AVX-512 support, 32 MB of L3 cache, and AES cryptographic instructions. Benchmark results place uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 206.52 GB/s and single-core stress-ng processing at 3016.68, reflecting strong execution efficiency within its segment. Multi-core performance is balanced, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 34399.09 and Redis SET operations of 34.09 million per second. With an approximate 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance emphasizes thread count and rapid disk I/O over massive memory capacity. The instance lacks bundled GPU acceleration and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and its shared CPU resource model presents occasional multi-tenant contention tradeoffs. It suits software build environments, CI/CD runners, web serving, and database workloads.
